## Hungarian armistice negotiations: troop departure and instructions requested

**Sources on this page:** p124 A1, p124 A2, p124 A3.

<a id="edition-cases-military-hungarian-armistice-instructions-hungarian-armistice-negotiations-troop-departure-and-instructions-requested"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p124 A1/A2/A3, PDF page 127, are one source-labeled three-part message:
`LP v NKJ (7.17 p.m., November 5th)`; `1715 (4/11) 3 TLE`.
The consecutive part labels and native lengths **352 / 266 / 48** establish
the assembly. All three use the unchanged published **Nov4–6** key.

<a id="source-p124-a1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-hungarian-armistice-instructions-p124-a1"></a>

### p124 A1

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/sources/p124_A1.png)
contains **352 valid coordinates** and **176 / 176 fixed plaintext positions**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 352-coordinate frame:**

```text
ANOXHXLXOPXHEERESGRUPPEKOOVESHATWAFFENSTILLSTANDSVERHANDLUNGENFDERUNGARISCHETRUPPENEINGELEITETXDEUTSCHETRUPPENSOLLENSOBALDALSMOEGLICHPNGARISCHENUNDSUEDSLAVISC3ENBODENVERLASSEN0
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
ANOXHXLXOPXHEERESGRUPPEKOOVESHATWAFFENSTILLSTANDSVERHANDLUNGENFUERUNGARISCHETRUPPENEINGELEITETXDEUTSCHETRUPPENSOLLENSOBALDALSMOEGLICHUNGARISCHENUNDSUEDSLAVISCHENBODENVERLASSEN0
```

</details>

The changes are source **80 G→A**, **110 F→V** and **306 X→V**. They
repair `FDER`, `PNGARISCHEN` and `SUEDSLAVISC3EN`. The name string
**KOOVES** and the final **0** are unchanged.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlauts; the literal closing 0 is retained:**

> An O. H. L. Op. Heeresgruppe KOOVES hat Waffenstillstandsverhandlungen
> für ungarische Truppen eingeleitet. Deutsche Truppen sollen sobald
> als möglich ungarischen und südslavischen Boden verlassen. 0.

The final 0 remains an uninterpreted label. The edition does not turn
KOOVES into an independently identified person's name. The message
reports negotiations and says German troops are to leave; it does not
show that the departure occurred.


**Cross-key phrase witness.** The unchanged [p117 C3 reading](117.md#edition-cases-military-nov3-withdrawal-and-night-report-p117-c3)
supplies the 59-letter phrase from `SOBALD` through `VERLASSEN` under the
separate Nov1–3 key. It independently supports A1's `UNGARISCHEN` and
`SUEDSLAVISCHEN` repairs: source **306 X→V** and **80 G→A** respectively.
The [paired-source certificate](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/withdrawal_parallel.json)
records all 59 positions and the original coordinate pairs. The verb remains
`SOLLEN` here and `WERDEN` in p117; the headers also differ. This is a
parallel phrase, with no extra recovered position or physical message.
The separate `FDER`→`FUER` repair remains a word proposal.

<a id="source-p124-a2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-hungarian-armistice-instructions-p124-a2"></a>

### p124 A2

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/sources/p124_A2.png)
contains **266 valid coordinates** and **133 / 133 fixed plaintext positions**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 266-coordinate frame:**

```text
AXOXKX11NSTBEAUFTRAGTXZWEIGENERLSTABSOFFIZIEREZUDENVERHANDLUNGENZUENTSENDENXWEISUNGENANAXJXKX11UNDHIER3ERFUERDIEVERHANDLUNGENERBETENX
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
AXOXKX11ISTBEAUFTRAGTXZWEIGENERLSTABSOFFIZIEREZUDENVERHANDLUNGENZUENTSENDENXWEISUNGENANAXOXKX11UNDHIERHERFUERDIEVERHANDLUNGENERBETENX
```

</details>

The changes are source **16 X→V**, **88 D→G** and **106 G→A**. They
repair `11NST`, the second `A J K` sequence, and `HIER3ER`. The first
`A O K 11` and both occurrences of 11 remain as already decoded.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and one explicitly supplied spelling letter in brackets:**

> A. O. K. 11 ist beauftragt, zwei Gener[a]lstabsoffiziere zu den
> Verhandlungen zu entsenden. Weisungen an A. O. K. 11 und hierher für
> die Verhandlungen erbeten.

The source-derived string is **GENERLSTABSOFFIZIERE**, with no A between
R and L. The bracketed A appears only in the readable display. It is not
a recovered plaintext position, an insertion into the cipher, or part of
the repair count. The message reports an assignment and requests
instructions; it does not state that the officers had already arrived.

<a id="edition-cases-military-hungarian-armistice-instructions-conditional-interpretation-and-source-defined-ocr-correction"></a>

### Conditional interpretation and source-defined OCR correction

Earlier OCR merged the second part with the first 40 coordinates of the
third part, introduced extra symbols into two groups, and omitted A3's
final **VDFFA FAA** row. The scan explicitly labels separate **2 TL**
and **3 TL** frames and supplies the eight omitted coordinates. The
[frozen OCR snapshot](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/ocr_snapshot.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/certificates.json)
replay the exact correction: two OCR-only symbol deletions, two resolved
OCR masks, the part boundary after 266 coordinates, and the visible A3
final row. A1's separate masked F at source index 194 is also resolved
visually. The old shared OCR corpus is unchanged.

These transcript corrections are distinct from the six proposed changes
to visible historical coordinates. Across the three records, **666 valid
coordinates** give **333 / 333 fixed positions** in the source-defined
frames. All three edited streams re-encrypt exactly. There are **six
observed-coordinate substitutions, zero fills and no historical source
insertions, deletions or key changes**. A2's bracketed display letter
adds nothing to those counts. The damaged separate p124 B is excluded.

A1's body already appeared in an earlier unreviewed repository candidate;
the old A2/A3 OCR artifacts and published key credit are also preserved.
This source edition makes no historical first-solution claim. See the
[inputs](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/inputs.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/README.md).


<a id="edition-cases-military-nov4-flying-unit-inquiry"></a>

## p124 B — Inquiry whether flying units should depart or remain; opening reference unresolved

**Edition context:** Flying units: should they depart or remain?.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov4-flying-unit-inquiry-flying-units-should-they-depart-or-remain"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p124 section B contains a short inquiry about whether flying units
should leave or remain. The source prints **183 slots**, including **25
masked coordinates**, against an advertised **184**. A visibly short
four-slot group constrains the proposed missing coordinate, and a conditional
184-slot frame yields **92 plaintext positions, 67 fixed raw**.

The edited reading repairs ordinary words in the body while leaving the
entire opening reference untouched. It has **83/92 fixed positions** and
requires **2 observed-coordinate substitutions, 16 source-mask fills and 1
inserted-slot fill**. The published **Nov4–6** key stays unchanged. The two
equally priced local gap positions are both retained.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p124_B_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/sources/p124_B_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
<a id="source-p124-b"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-nov4-flying-unit-inquiry-p124-b"></a>

### p124 B

[Reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — header:**

```text
Page heading: 4th NOVEMBER, 1918.
B) UKH v ZON (4.41 a.m., November ---)
RICHI-184
```

</details>

The intercept's day is missing and remains missing. The 4 November page
heading is a separate source layer. The [literal input](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/inputs.json)
preserves every dash and the invalid printed `U` in `GXXGU`.

The short **XFVV** group occupies source indices **15–18**. The displayed
frame inserts an unknown coordinate at **source boundary 17**, before
original source index 17. No source slot is removed or reordered.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 184-slot frame, boundary 17; 67/92 fixed positions:**

```text
??ERX?K??1?2??OP??ICHT?E??T?ENDLI??XXSOLLEN?LI?GERA??EI?UNG?N?B?LIEGENX?DERHIERRLEIBENXFRAGE
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame; 2 observed-coordinate substitutions, 16 source-mask fills and 1 added-slot fill; 83/92 fixed positions:**

```text
??ERX?K??1?2??OP?NICHTVERSTAENDLICHXXSOLLENFLIEGERABTEILUNGENABFLIEGENXODERHIERBLEIBENXFRAGE
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete edited stream; the opening token stays literal:**

> ??ERX?K??1?2??OP?. Nicht verstaendlich. Sollen Fliegerabteilungen abfliegen oder hierbleiben. Frage.

The initial **17 positions** are unchanged, including **nine unresolved
positions** and the labels **1** and **2**. No addressee, serial or office is
inferred from that fragment. The literal word **Frage** stays visible at
the end; it is not silently replaced by punctuation.

**Meaning:** The proposed body says that a communication is not understood
and asks whether flying units should depart by air or remain here. It does
not identify the units or establish that either action occurred. These are
explicit word restorations from a damaged source, not a complete recovery
of its opening reference.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov4-flying-unit-inquiry-repair-account"></a>

### Repair account

The two changes to observed coordinates, using zero-based original source
indices, are **14 G→D** and **171 A→G**. The latter repairs raw
`HIERRLEIBEN` to proposed `HIERBLEIBEN`; the former helps supply `B` in
`FLIEGERABTEILUNGEN` at a position whose other coordinate was already masked.

| Kind | Original source indices and supplied values |
| --- | --- |
| Observed-coordinate substitutions | 14 G→D; 171 A→G |
| Printed-mask fills | 7→A; 23→F; 33→F; 58 U→A; 66→X; 67→G; 68→A; 88→G; 102→A; 103→G; 135→X; 146→A; 147→V; 170→G; 175→A; 176→X |
| Added-slot fill | F at source boundary 17, model index 17 |
| Unfilled printed masks | 9, retained in the opening fragment |

All listed mask fills except source 58 fill printed dashes. Source 58 is the
invalid printed `U`, retained literally in the source transcript. The
certificate records each event with its original glyph, source index,
model index and resulting plaintext domain. Filling remaining masks with a
mechanical value produces a complete re-encryption witness, explicitly
marked **nonhistorical**; it does not supply the opening reference.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov4-flying-unit-inquiry-both-local-gap-minima"></a>

### Both local gap minima

The verifier compares all five insertion boundaries within or at the edges
of the visibly four-slot group, against the same partial edited template:

| Source boundary | Observed substitutions | Printed-mask fills | Added-slot fills |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 15 | 3 | 16 | 1 |
| 16 | 2 | 16 | 1 |
| 17 | 2 | 16 | 1 |
| 18 | 3 | 16 | 1 |
| 19 | 3 | 16 | 1 |

Boundaries **16 and 17 tie**. Both add F next to the already printed F,
producing the same edited ciphertext group **XFFVV** and the same edited
plaintext. Their unfilled raw frames differ because the unknown slot lies
on opposite sides of the observed F.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — equally priced boundary-16 alternative; 67/92 fixed positions:**

```text
??ERX?K??1?2??OP??ICHT?E??T?ENDLI??XXSOLLEN?LI?GER???EI?UNGEN?B?LIEGENX?DERHIERRLEIBENXFRAGE
```

</details>

The displayed boundary-17 frame is a presentation choice. The certificate
preserves both mappings and all five price comparisons. The comparison is
limited to this stated short-group family and fixed body proposal; it
neither proves a unique historical reading nor identifies the historical
stage at which the coordinate was lost.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov4-flying-unit-inquiry-source-restoration-attribution-and-reproduction"></a>

### Source restoration, attribution and reproduction

Earlier repository OCR contained **178 slots**: it omitted the printed
last-row `---AV` group and misread or masked several observed coordinates.
The reviewed **183-slot transcription** restores those actual source marks.
Those machine-input corrections are separate from the one missing
coordinate hypothesized in `XFVV`.

J. Rives Childs's scan is the historical source. The period-key work of
George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, Lasry's 2017 key list,
and earlier repository work retain their credit. The frozen earlier OCR
and recomputed unchanged-key output are available in
[prior candidates](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/prior_candidates.json).
No first-decipherment priority is claimed.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/certificates.json),
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/README.md)
include every raw domain, both minimal source mappings, all repair events,
